findings.title: Cleanup ticker interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The ticker is reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute with no mention in the PR description. It looks like a debugging leftover. All cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, annotations, query history, and others) will now run 10x more often. That adds database load, and the annotation cleanup now issues many more round trips per run. clean() also has a 9-minute timeout, so runs can overlap or queue up. Revert to 10 minutes.

findings.title: Debug logging at Error level, logging full ID lists every batch
findings.body: Every batch calls r.log.Error(...) with the full `ids` slice and the SQL condition, both before and after the delete. This happens in the time-based and count-based annotation paths and in CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags (lines 554, 557, 576, 579). Healthy cleanup runs will emit Error-level log lines, which triggers alerting and pollutes logs. With large batch sizes (e.g. 32767), each line contains tens of thousands of IDs. This is clearly leftover debug output and should be removed or lowered to Debug, without dumping the ID list.

findings.title: SQLite parameter-limit check uses configured batch size and a stale 999 limit
findings.body: The inline-ID branch is chosen from the configured batch size, not from len(ids). When the batch size is above 999 it inlines IDs. Otherwise it uses placeholders, and those are limited only by the batch size, so this part is fine. However, the 999 limit is the pre-3.32 default, so newer SQLite builds pay for building a huge string for no reason. The inline path also builds the string with repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation, which is O(n^2) for 32k IDs. Use strings.Builder, or chunk by len(ids).

findings.title: Orphan tag query: unqualified annotation_id and LIMIT inside the NOT EXISTS condition
findings.body: The condition is `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM annotation a WHERE annotation_id = a.id) LIMIT n`. It is appended as `SELECT id FROM annotation_tag WHERE ... LIMIT n`. That works syntactically, but the unqualified `annotation_id` relies on name resolution to the outer table. If the batch always returns the same orphan IDs and the delete affects 0 rows, the loop ends, which is fine. A real concern: annotation_tag may have no `id` column in some schemas (the original query also used `id`), so the behaviour is the same as before. Mainly, the unqualified column should be `annotation_tag.annotation_id` for clarity and safety.

findings.title: Raw string-concatenated condition passed to fetchIDs relies on annotationType being a trusted fragment
findings.body: fetchIDs interpolates an arbitrary SQL condition into the query and also inserts the table name. The callers pass in annotationType, which is an SQL fragment, via Sprintf. This was already the case before, but it is now a generic helper that accepts unvalidated SQL strings. The empty-condition check is the only guard. This is fragile, though currently inputs are internal constants.

findings.title: Large test creates 40k annotations, which is slow, and the test name claims a SQLite version condition that is not enforced
findings.body: The new case inserts 40003 annotations and 80k tag rows, and the shared fakeSQL runs on whichever DB is configured. The name refers to 'SQLite >= 3.32.0', but nothing is checked. It also does not cover the non-SQLite placeholder path with a large batch (e.g. MySQL or Postgres parameter limits of 65535). Batch 32767 with placeholders is fine, but a batch above 65535 is untested.
